before: Runtime baseline: 1 playback control passes and chapter-clock test fails. Six known-movie controls and all 18 actual software playback controls pass.
change: For unknown/zero mvhd duration, chapter clock selection prefers known tkhd movie-clock presentation duration while preserving the decode-duration floor. If track presentation duration is also unstated, use a nominal composition endpoint including the final equal-PTS group. after: 45 distinct checks pass across 8 targets, including 2 new tests. Eighteen synthetic movies preserve 200/220/240ms chapter names/moments in both supported clocks and both parser wrappers, exact software YUV/RGB, 260ms native duration, 180 seek positions, rewind and EOF. fixtures: 22 byte-identical regenerated files: 18 own short colored VP9 movies, 3 analytic YUV16 oracles and manifest. No private media/parameters, external encoder, FFmpeg or network; ordinary tests read saved assets only.
limitations: The clock-selection heuristic remains compatibility behavior for two authored chpl conventions; ambiguous small timestamps cannot always distinguish clocks.
With all presentation headers unstated, the endpoint is a nominal index estimate and cannot prove display output from decode-only packets.
No new visual UI, performance, full-project green or GPU parity claim. Historical unrelated baseline failures remain separate.
